trigger: a healthy server running only e.g. noop reap passes, every other result label boot-seeded and flat at zero
summary: YuzuResponseReapNotRunning had no sum()/aggregation over the result-labeled reap counter, so every boot-seeded-but-quiet result label independently satisfied ==0 and the alert fired permanently on every healthy install. Independently re-derived and empirically confirmed via live promtool simulation by both sre (Gate 6) and enterprise-readiness (Gate 6, 5 concurrent firing instances against 5h of simulated healthy data).

adjudicated_by: orchestrator (chaos-injector's live-measured HIGH taken as the governing band over performance's original MEDIUM)
trigger: sustained high-facet-cardinality ingest whose TTL clustering puts >kReapFacetDeleteBatchRows facets in one reap chunk, under real pool contention
summary: Chunking the parent-row count alone did not bound the CASCADE's own latency to response_facets, which has no LIMIT of its own -- up to 2.5M child-row deletes in one implicit statement. MEASURED by performance at 1997ms/2000ms budget under realistic load, then independently reproduced live against PostgreSQL 18.4 by chaos-injector (~1929ms on an IDLE database for the max-cardinality case) and elevated to HIGH via the self-sustaining-wedge mechanism: a statement_timeout failure rolls back the WHOLE pass and the deterministic ORDER BY re-selects the identical backlog next pass. Also raised by unhappy-path (UP-1/UP-2) via the same compounding analysis.

limit=0 semantics shifted during the PG rewrite (was previously treated as "use the default page size" on the SQLite path in at least one caller convention); not independently re-verified as a regression, recorded as a NICE-level naming/semantics note.

adjudicated_by: orchestrator (confirmed the NUL-truncation mechanism is real via pg::exec_params paramLengths=nullptr; confirmed the exact vulnerable call site agent_service_impl.cpp:1222 is byte-identical to origin/dev, i.e. the CALLING code is pre-existing; confirmed the same truncate-at-NUL behaviour existed on the SQLite path too via sqlite3_bind_text(...,-1,...); judged in-scope for this PR anyway because ADR-0039's own posture text, authored this session, makes an affirmatively false safety claim for exactly this input class -- an I6(a) false-assurance case -- and because six sibling PG stores in this codebase already carry the equivalent guard this store never got
trigger: a compromised or malicious enrolled agent sends a CommandResponse whose command_id contains an embedded NUL byte
summary: instruction_id/execution_id/plugin were bound unsanitized via pg::exec_params, which binds every parameter as a NUL-terminated C string (paramLengths=nullptr) -- an embedded NUL silently truncates the bound value instead of failing the INSERT (unlike invalid UTF-8, which does fail it, the case ADR-0039's own text discusses). Independently found by compliance-officer (F1) and chaos-injector (Finding 2, which refined the mechanism: not literal impersonation since truncation only yields a prefix match, but real identity-aliasing + audit/log divergence between the full command_id captured in spdlog/AnalyticsEvent and the truncated stored value). Fixed by rejecting (fail-soft-drop, counted via a new malformed_identity_field reason) rather than truncating, matching the sibling-store convention and restoring the ADR's own originally-intended fail-soft-drop guarantee for malformed identity fields -- this also fully closes chaos-injector's audit-divergence angle, since nothing is stored under a wrong/truncated id anymore.

trigger: ResponseStore pool degrades mid-call on query_responses, the aggregate tool (2 branches), get_bundle_result, or the two new REST bundle/visualization degrade sites
summary: All 4 new MCP branches and 2 new REST routes added for ResponseStore degrade omitted retry_after_ms, leaving the A4 envelope's retryability signal null for a condition this PR itself documents as retryable -- contradicting the a4_error lambda's own doc comment and the established REST precedent (retry_after_ms:5000 on the sibling /sle/agents/{id} store-degrade 503). Independently re-derived HIGH by sre via I4 (harmful operator/caller guidance) -- an agentic caller following the documented A4 contract would treat a transient blip as terminal.

render_filter_bar's per-column facet_values() read silently rendered an empty "All" dropdown on a degraded read -- indistinguishable from a column that genuinely has no other values -- right next to a results table that correctly banners the same degrade. Also independently found by chaos-injector during its degrade-signal-propagation sweep (graded LOW/INFO there, not formally raised as a separate finding).

trigger: an out-of-cohort or otherwise unrelated response's instruction_id happens to match a real dispatched one, with no dispatch-binding check at the ResponseStore/BundleOrchestrator read seam
summary: No code path validates that a response's instruction_id was ever dispatched to the reporting agent_id -- ResponseStore is trusted as sole source of truth for that binding everywhere except Preflight's cohort-scoped grid. Explicitly out of this PR's diff (bundle_orchestrator.cpp's trust-relevant collate/query_by_execution logic is untouched by this PR), pre-existing, unrelated to the NUL-truncation mechanism (UP-5) once that is fixed. Recommend filing as a standalone follow-up issue.

trigger: a reap pass regularly lands near/over the 2000ms budget under sustained near-cap facet cardinality even after the facet-cascade fix
summary: Fixed cadence (~60m) with no backoff/catch-up after a capped pass; real drain throughput may be a small fraction of the nominal 10,000-row/pass cap under sustained load. Substantially mitigated by the facet-cascade-bounding fix (perf-F1) reducing per-chunk worst-case latency, but the adaptive-cadence recommendation itself was not implemented this round.

trigger: ResponseStore pool degrades for the entire duration of a preflight run's window, not merely a transient blip
summary: any_check_degraded() skips the whole tick with no independent staleness escalation once past deadline; a sustained (not transient) outage leaves a run 'running' indefinitely with the same generic banner whether the outage is 10s or 10h old. Mitigated: deployment_routes.cpp does not require run.status==complete, so Deploy can still act on the accumulated go/warn cohort; the run itself is not eternal (prune_older_than has no status filter, vanishes at the 14-day cutoff).

"Consider a shorter response_retention_days" is factually wrong -- steady-state expiry rate tracks ingest rate, not the retention window, so shortening it does not relieve a cap-hitting backlog. Fixed with the same sum()-gap fix (arch-F1), corrected to the AuditStore sibling's honest framing (engineering escalation, not a config change).

summary: No Postgres capacity/sizing guidance specific to response_store, unlike audit-log.md's parallel #capacity section referenced from its own alert runbook.
